basics.description: **Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel: one-deploy solution** Abstract Security: a security data pipeline and agentic SIEM in one platform. One Azure deployment that creates the Data Collection Endpoint, Data Collection Rule and tables that Abstract Security sends events to through the Logs Ingestion API, and installs Microsoft Sentinel content for that data. **Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel** sets up, in one deployment, everything Abstract needs to deliver data into Microsoft Sentinel. Choose the resource group that holds your Sentinel workspace, or a new one. Every field below explains what it sets, when to change it and what follows.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: What: the region of a new workspace and of the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule. With an existing workspace, the endpoint and rule follow the workspace's region whatever is chosen here.

options.text: Pick what to set up below, and the form shows only the tabs and fields that choice needs. The full set is the Log Analytics workspace (new or yours), the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule Abstract sends to, the AbstractEventLogs_CL table, optional routes into the Microsoft ASIM tables, a data-lake table and vendor tables, the Abstract content (data connector page, parser, analytics rules, hunting queries, workbooks, playbooks and automation rules) and the read-only discovery inventory. Have ready: Contributor and User Access Administrator (or Owner) on the resource group, and the Abstract app registration if Abstract has already given you one.

basics.name: choice
basics.label: What do you want to set up?
basics.toolTip: What: picks the parts of Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel this deployment sets up. Every tab and field the choice does not use is hidden, and its part is not deployed. When: 'Data plane + content' is the usual first install; 'Discovery only' inventories an existing workspace without changing it; 'Content only' adds the content to a workspace whose data plane an earlier deployment created; 'Custom' lets you tick the parts. Consequence: you can run the deployment again later with another choice; parts already deployed are kept. Portal: Resource groups > this group > Deployments lists each run.

ASIM (the Advanced Security Information Model) is Microsoft's common schema. Writing Abstract events into Microsoft's ASim tables means the ASIM analytics rules, hunting queries and workbooks already in the workspace see Abstract data with no change. Each schema adds one dataflow to the rule.

elements.name: enableAsim
elements.label: Write mapped events into Microsoft's ASIM tables
elements.toolTip: What: an extra route per chosen schema that maps matching events into that schema's ASim table. When: turn on if your SOC uses ASIM content or Microsoft solutions built on it. Consequence: expect new alerts from ASIM rules, and duplicates where a Microsoft connector already collects the same vendor. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables, the ASim tables.

elements.name: asimSchemas
elements.label: ASIM schemas
elements.toolTip: What: the schemas to write, one ASim table each. Consequence: one dataflow per schema (Azure allows 20 per rule). When: keep all eight unless a Microsoft connector already fills a schema. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables.

allowedValues.label: AuditEvent (ASimAuditEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Configuration changes, admin actions and audit trails from any product Abstract normalises.

allowedValues.label: Authentication (ASimAuthenticationEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Sign-ins, logons, MFA prompts and their failures. Feeds the identity analytics most SOCs rely on.

allowedValues.label: Dns (ASimDnsActivityLogs)
allowedValues.description: DNS queries and responses from resolvers, firewalls and secure-web gateways.

allowedValues.label: FileEvent (ASimFileEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: File create, modify, rename, delete and read events from EDR and file-integrity sources.

allowedValues.label: NetworkSession (ASimNetworkSessionLogs)
allowedValues.description: Firewall, flow and connection events. Usually the largest schema by volume.

allowedValues.label: ProcessEvent (ASimProcessEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Process creation and termination from EDR and OS audit sources.

allowedValues.label: RegistryEvent (ASimRegistryEventLogs)
allowedValues.description: Windows registry key and value changes from EDR sources.

allowedValues.label: WebSession (ASimWebSessionLogs)
allowedValues.description: HTTP requests seen by proxies, WAFs and secure-web gateways.

elements.name: excludeAsimFromAbstractTable
elements.label: One copy: keep ASIM-mapped events out of AbstractEventLogs_CL
elements.toolTip: What: an event an ASIM route takes is stored once, in its ASim table, instead of twice. When: turn on to halve the ingestion of mapped events. Consequence: your own queries that read only AbstractEventLogs_CL stop seeing those events; this solution's analytics rules read both. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Logs, query AbstractEventLogs_CL.

elements.name: apiKeyMode
elements.label: Store my Abstract API key now
elements.toolTip: What: where the playbooks read the Abstract API key at run time. 'In a new Key Vault' creates a vault in this resource group and writes the key you enter below into it; 'In an existing Key Vault' writes it into a vault in this resource group; 'I already have a secret' points the playbooks at a secret you made yourself; 'Later' leaves it empty and asks for nothing, so the deployment never waits on a key. When: choose one of the first two when you have the key to hand, the third if it already sits in a vault. Consequence: with the first two the deployment also grants each playbook the two roles it needs (switch below), and the key travels only as a secure parameter, never in the outputs or the deployment history; until a secret is set, the playbooks fail at their first Abstract call. On a rerun, Later keeps the secret the installed playbooks read now (the form reads it from Abstract-Enrich-Incident). Portal: Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets.

elements.name: kvMode
elements.label: Your Abstract API key secret
elements.toolTip: What: how to find the secret you made yourself. The key itself never enters this deployment. When: 'Pick a secret' lists vaults and their secrets; 'Enter the URI' for a vault you cannot list. Consequence: a wrong secret fails each playbook at its first Abstract call. When: you chose 'I already have a secret' above. Portal: Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets.

elements.name: kvSelector
elements.label: Key Vault
elements.toolTip: What: the vaults in your subscriptions that you can see. Pick the one that holds (or will hold) the Abstract API key. Consequence: none on the vault; the deployment does not change it. When: keep the API key in one vault you control. Portal: Key vaults.

elements.name: kvSecret
elements.label: Secret holding the Abstract API key
elements.toolTip: What: the vault's secrets, listed through Azure Resource Manager (names and URIs only; values are never read). Consequence: the playbooks read the latest version of this secret on every run, so rotating the key needs no redeploy. When: pick the secret that holds the Abstract API key. Portal: Key vault > Objects > Secrets.

elements.name: lookbackHours
elements.label: Enrich-incident lookback
elements.toolTip: What: how far back the Enrich-incident playbook searches Abstract for related events. Consequence: a longer window finds more context and takes longer to run. When: 24 hours suits most SOCs. Portal: Logic app > Parameters.

elements.name: deployPlaybookAutomationRules
elements.label: Automation rules that run Verdict and Tune at source
elements.toolTip: What: two automation rules that run the Verdict and Tune-at-source playbooks on new incidents. Consequence: the deployment FAILS unless Microsoft Sentinel's own app (Azure Security Insights) holds 'Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor' on this resource group, granted about 10 minutes earlier. The form checks for that role below. When: only after the role above has been granted. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Automation.

Discovery is read-only. It reads the workspace's tables, ingestion volume, connectors, data collection rules, analytics rules, hunting queries, workbooks and playbooks, and writes a zip, one CSV per area and a self-contained HTML report to a storage account in this resource group. It creates a user-assigned managed identity with read-only roles (Log Analytics Reader on the workspace, Reader on the subscription unless you turn that off), the storage account and two short deployment scripts, and runs for 5 to 15 minutes. Nothing in the workspace changes. Find the report afterwards: Storage accounts > the account > Containers > sentinel-discovery.

elements.name: discoveryDays
elements.label: Look-back window
elements.toolTip: What: how many days back discovery reads table volume, ingestion health, agents and rule activity, 1 to 90. When: 30 days evens out weekly patterns; use 7 to 14 on a very busy workspace. Consequence: a longer window makes the queries slower and scans more data. Portal: the report's header states the window it used.

elements.name: discoveryDeviceDays
elements.label: Sender breakdown window
elements.toolTip: What: the window for the CEF and Syslog sender breakdowns, 1 to 7 days. When: leave at 1 unless senders vary by weekday. Consequence: these scan the raw CommonSecurityLog and Syslog tables, so each extra day adds query time and cost on a busy workspace. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables shows those tables' size.

elements.name: discoveryProfileTopTables
elements.label: Largest tables to profile
elements.toolTip: What: how many of the largest Analytics-plan tables discovery breaks down by two columns, 0 to 50. When: raise it to profile more of a long tail of tables; 0 turns the breakdown off. Consequence: each table adds one query. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Tables, sorted by size.

elements.name: discoverySkipRuleQueryText
elements.label: Leave analytics rule KQL out of the output
elements.toolTip: What: leaves the KQL text of analytics rules out of the output; which rule reads which table is still recorded. When: your policy does not allow detection logic in a file, even in your own storage account. Consequence: the report cannot show rule logic. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Analytics lists the rules.

elements.name: discoverySkipContentQueryText
elements.label: Leave function, hunting and saved-search KQL out of the output
elements.toolTip: What: leaves the KQL text of functions, hunting queries and saved searches out of the output; which content reads which table is still recorded. When: the same policy as for rule text. Consequence: the report cannot show that logic. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Hunting, and Logs > Functions.

elements.name: discoveryDeployWorkbook
elements.label: Also install the discovery template's inventory workbook
elements.toolTip: What: installs the discovery template's own inventory workbook, Sentinel inventory (<workspace>), as the standalone discovery template does. When: on by default; clear it to keep only the Sentinel Discovery workbook the Content tab installs. Consequence: on, both workbooks are installed and show much the same inventory. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Workbooks > My workbooks.

elements.name: discoveryAssignSubscriptionReader
elements.label: Grant the discovery identity Reader on this subscription
elements.toolTip: What: gives the discovery identity Reader on this subscription, so it can list data collection rules, endpoints, Sentinel workbooks and playbooks. When: keep on unless policy forbids subscription-wide Reader. Consequence: off, those areas are recorded as not read and the report has gaps. Portal: Subscriptions > the subscription > Access control (IAM).

elements.name: discoveryGrantDeployerBlobRead
elements.label: Let me open the report (Storage Blob Data Reader for the deployer)
elements.toolTip: What: gives you, the person deploying, Storage Blob Data Reader on the report container. When: keep on. Consequence: shared keys are off on the storage account, so without it even an Owner cannot open the report until someone grants a data role. Portal: Storage accounts > the account > Access control (IAM).

elements.name: discoveryStorageAccountName
elements.label: Report storage account name
elements.toolTip: What: the storage account the report is written to, 3 to 24 lowercase letters and digits, unique in Azure. When: set it to follow a naming standard; empty generates one. Consequence: the account is created with public blob access and shared-key access off. Portal: Storage accounts > the account > Containers > sentinel-discovery. Example: abstractdiscovery01.

validations.message: 3 to 24 lowercase letters and digits, or empty.

elements.placeholder: Leave empty to generate a name

elements.name: discoveryRbacWaitMinutes
elements.label: Wait for new roles
elements.toolTip: What: how long discovery waits for its new role assignments to take effect before failing, 1 to 45 minutes. When: raise it if a run failed with an authorization error right after the roles were granted. Consequence: the wait only lasts until the roles work. Portal: Resource groups > this group > Deployments shows the run.

elements.name: discoverySendToAbstract
elements.label: Send a copy of the output to Abstract
elements.toolTip: What: sends a copy of the output to Abstract. Exactly two files leave your tenant over HTTPS: inventory.zip and report.html. When: only when Abstract asked for it and gave you a SAS URL. Consequence: off keeps everything in your storage account. Portal: the copy goes to the container the SAS URL names.

elements.name: discoveryAbstractSasUrl
elements.toolTip: What: the HTTPS SAS URL of the container Abstract gave you, with write permission on that container only. When: only with the copy to Abstract turned on. Consequence: a wrong or expired URL fails the upload at the end of the run; the report in your account is still written. Portal: none; Abstract sends it to you. It is a secret: anyone holding it can write to that container until it expires.

constraints.validationMessage: An https:// SAS URL, as Abstract gave it.
